The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 68d6affc8c3cc3bc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 55. statement: Fix bounded velocity, domain, ball, and neighborhood constants, a richness constant cr > 0, an angular constant Ca > 0, exponents Ar, Aa ≥ 0, and η > 0. There are constants A∗, C∗, C′ depending only on these fixed data such that the following holds whenever X ≥ 2 and H ≥ C∗XA∗ . Let ν be a nonnegative measure supported in a ball of radius O(H), with ν(B(q, r)) ≤ Cbr2 (r ≥ 1). Let T be a finite family of lines ℓT = {(bT + 2ωT t, t) : t ∈ R}, |ωT | ≤ Cv, viewed as unit-width tubes over a fixed time interval of length O(H) containing the time projection of supp ν. Write dT (x, t) = |x − bT − 2ωT t| and eT = (2ωT , 1)/|(2ωT , 1)|. Assume: (i) Every tube is rich against ν: Z (1 + dT (q))−M dν(q) ≥ crHX−Ar , M = 100. (7.1) (ii) At ν-almost every q there is a measurably chosen probability (pT (q))T∈T , supported on tubes with dT (q) ≤ Cn, such that every spherical direction ball satisfies X eT ∈BS2 (e,r) pT (q) ≤ CaXAa rη (r ≥ H−1 ). (7.2) Then each tube can be assigned to one of at most XC′ plates (planes thickened by XC′ ). Its assigned plate contains its central line segment over the relevant time interval. If n is a unit normal to that plate, then |n · (2ωT , 1)| ≤ XC′ /H. (7.3) The constants are independent of the number of tubes. In particular, the richness in (7.1) and the pointwise law in (7.2) use exactly the same measure ν.
